## Context

Parent epic `a4bd-4ca8-c44f-49bb`; depends on S1 (`248f-ac00-18db-4259`), which adds the
peer-confirmation store and records a confirmation when WE push a link. This story adds the
second, independent evidence source: a link observed in an authoritative remote snapshot is
peer-confirmed even if this clone never pushed it (peer-created links, links pushed before the
store existed, links pushed by another clone).

The epic's binding constraint: **a partial / paginated / failed / stale read is NON-EVIDENCE** —
it can neither confirm nor deny. rebar already has exactly this completeness signal, and this
story consumes it rather than inventing one. `fetcher.py::merge_issuelinks_map` writes the
per-issue `issuelinks` key ONLY on an authoritative read — an absent key means UNOBSERVED
(truncated page walk, HTTP 410, failed enrichment, a backend without `get_issuelinks_map`),
while `[]` means authoritatively-empty. This is the same G1 signal the inbound removal differ
already depends on. `BackendPaginationStallError` re-raises rather than degrading, so a stalled
pager never reaches this code as a complete read.

There is no snapshot revision counter in the codebase; `pass_id` is the only handle (epic
comment D3), so records store `confirmed_pass`, not an ordered revision. No ordering logic is
built on it.

## Scope

- `peer_confirmations.py` — add
  `confirm_from_snapshot(store, curr_snapshot, binding_store, pass_id) -> int`, returning the
  number of records written.
  - Iterate `curr_snapshot` entries. **Process an entry ONLY if `"issuelinks" in entry`** — an
    absent key is UNOBSERVED and must be skipped whole. Use the `in` test, never
    `entry.get("issuelinks") or []`, which collapses observed-empty into unobserved (the exact
    trap `inbound_differ.py`'s G1 docstring warns about).
  - Source local id is `binding_store.get_local_id(jira_key)`; skip the entry when it is None.
  - For each raw link entry use `link_direction.resolve_inbound_link(link)` to get
    `(other_key, relation)` in LOCAL relation vocabulary, then
    `binding_store.get_local_id(other_key)` for the target. Skip entries where either is None.
    `resolve_inbound_link` is used directly rather than `observed_peer_deps` because the latter
    returns only `(relation, target)` and DISCARDS the vendor link id this story must persist.
  - Record each as `direction="snapshot"`, `source="snapshot"`, `link_id=link.get("id")`,
    `confirmed_pass=pass_id`.
- `reconcile.py::_persist_and_log` — call it inside the existing `if persist:` block, as a
  sibling of the `_advance_baselines(binding_store, ctx.curr_snapshot, ctx.synced_fields)` call
  and BEFORE `binding_store.save()`, wrapped in the same fail-open `try/except Exception` shape
  that call already uses (log to stderr, never break a sync pass). Then `store.save()`.
- Confirmation is monotonic and additive: observing a link confirms it; NOT observing it never
  un-confirms. Un-confirmation is deliberately excluded — it would reintroduce "absence is
  evidence", the exact failure the epic forbids.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1 A snapshot entry with `issuelinks` present and a bound link produces a record with
      `direction="snapshot"`, `source="snapshot"`, `link_id` from the raw entry's `id`, and the
      current `pass_id`. Proof:
      `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/apply/test_peer_confirmations_snapshot.py -k observed`.
- [ ] AC2 A snapshot entry with the `issuelinks` key ABSENT produces NO record for that issue,
      even when the link is present and managed locally. Proof:
      `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/apply/test_peer_confirmations_snapshot.py -k unobserved`.
- [ ] AC3 An authoritative `issuelinks: []` produces no record and does NOT remove or invalidate
      an existing confirmation. Proof:
      `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/apply/test_peer_confirmations_snapshot.py -k empty_authoritative`.
- [ ] AC4 A link whose source or target key is unbound is skipped — no record, no raise. Proof:
      `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/apply/test_peer_confirmations_snapshot.py -k unbound`.
- [ ] AC5 Relation mapping goes through `link_direction`, so an INWARD `Blocks` entry is recorded
      under `depends_on`, not `blocks`. Proof:
      `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/apply/test_peer_confirmations_snapshot.py -k direction`.
- [ ] AC6 An exception raised inside snapshot confirmation is logged and the reconcile pass still
      completes and persists (injected raising store). Proof:
      `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/apply/test_peer_confirmations_snapshot.py -k fail_open`.
- [ ] AC7 In no-write mode (`persist` False) no confirmation is written. Proof:
      `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/apply/test_peer_confirmations_snapshot.py -k nowrite`.
- [ ] AC8 Every edited module stays under the 800-line cap. Proof: `bash -c 'git archive HEAD |
      tar -xO src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/reconcile.py | wc -l'` per edited file, < 800.
- [ ] AC9 Gates green. Proof: `make lint` exit 0, `make typecheck` exit 0,
      `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler` exit 0.

## Testing

- New suite `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/apply/test_peer_confirmations_snapshot.py` covering the
  observed / unobserved / authoritative-empty trichotomy, unbound source and target, inward
  direction mapping, fail-open behavior, and the no-write path.
- Regression: `make lint && make typecheck && pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler` — this story is
  additive and must not change any differ or apply behavior.

## Out of scope

The removal decline (S3) and the upgrade backfill (S4). No un-confirmation. No new fetch — this
story consumes `ctx.curr_snapshot` as already fetched.
